Document Title: Dynamic Hierarchical Posterior Evolution for Bayesian Neural Network-Based Industrial Digital Twins under Non-Stationary Conditions
Authors: C. Li; L. Wang; L. Xu; Y. Liu; Y. Kong; X. Song
Author Affiliations: Henan University of Science and Technology, Luoyang, China; Luoyang Sunrui Wanji Titanium Industry Co., Ltd., Luoyang, China; Luoyang Sunrui Wanji Titanium Industry Co., Ltd., Luoyang, China; Henan University of Science and Technology, Luoyang, China; Huanghe University of Science and Technology, Zhengzhou, China; Henan University of Science and Technology, Luoyang, China
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Symposium on Computer Technology and Information Science (ISCTIS)
Abstract: Industrial digital twins must continuously ingest online data during long-term operation and revise the virtual-to-physical mapping under non-stationary factors such as operating-condition switching, equipment degradation, and observation bias. Conventional deterministic models cannot explicitly characterize predictive uncertainty, while existing Bayesian continual-learning methods still suffer from weak historical knowledge retention, limited physical-consistency constraints, and degraded uncertainty quality under drift. To address these issues, this paper proposes Dynamic Hierarchical Posterior Evolution (DHPE) for non-stationary industrial digital twins. In the representation layer, a hierarchical Gaussian-Inv-Gamma formulation with dynamic scale adjustment is introduced to maintain uncertainty health during online updating. In the evolution layer, complex posteriors are projected into Gaussian-mixture interface posteriors, and geometric Wasserstein distance is used to jointly incorporate historical posterior inheritance and physically anchored priors, thereby enabling smooth recursion under non-Gaussian conditions while preserving long-term physical consistency. A closed-loop mechanism integrating drift monitoring, state switching, and geometric feedback is further constructed to adaptively regulate inheritance strength, anchoring stiffness, and uncertainty width. Online experiments on titanium reduction furnace temperature prediction under three representative non-stationary scenarios show that DHPE delivers more stable error trajectories, more reasonable interval coverage, and more consistent probabilistic predictions, while maintaining strong posterior recovery capability and long-term robustness.
Author Keywords: Industrial Digital Twin;Bayesian Neural Networks (BNN);online posterior evolution;physically anchored prior;Wasserstein distance;uncertainty quantification

Document Title: Adaptive Weighted Physical Prior Bayesian Neural Network for Industrial Digital Twins
Authors: C. Li; Y. Kong; Y. Liu; X. Song; Y. Ma; Q. Yue
Author Affiliations: Henan University of Science and Technology, Luoyang, China; Huanghe University of Science and Technology, Zhengzhou, China; Henan University of Science and Technology, Luoyang, China; Henan University of Science and Technology, Luoyang, China; Henan University of Science and Technology, Luoyang, China; Henan University of Science and Technology, Luoyang, China
Publication Title: 2025 6th International Conference on Information Science, Parallel and Distributed Systems (ISPDS)
Abstract: In the task of temperature prediction for the metallurgical industry within the context of industrial digital twins, Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) can effectively enhance model accuracy by incorporating physical prior information, though prior construction poses significant challenges. Drawing inspiration from Physics-Informed neural networks (PINNs), this paper centers domain knowledge as the core of “prior construction.” By transforming physical constraints into loss functions through variational inference, prior specification is converted into a constrained optimization problem. However, in multi-physics coupling modeling, the disparity in gradient magnitudes and convergence rates among constraints like energy conservation and heat transfer boundaries can lead to optimization imbalances, coupled with unstable updates of mean and variance parameters. To address this, we propose a novel framework: based on Wasserstein distance variational inference, it first employs a Hessian-based adaptive weight scheduling mechanism (Hessian-AWM) to dynamically balance multiconstraint weights. Second, it introduces a freeze-thaw training strategy to optimize mean and variance in phases, ensuring stable convergence. In titanium smelting furnace temperature prediction experiments, this framework achieves approximately 16.6% higher accuracy than the fixed-weight BNN baseline model and outperforms multiple mainstream methods. Ablation experiments further validate its effectiveness in balancing constraints and suppressing variance oscillations, providing a feasible pathway for constructing reliable priors in industrial BNNs.
Author Keywords: Industrial Digital Twin;Bayesian Neural Networks (BNN);Physics-Informed Prior;Wasserstein-2 variational inference;Adaptive Loss Weighting

Document Title: Water-Quality Digital Twins: A Review of Architectures, State-Space Assimilation, and Alerting
Author Affiliations: Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Karpagam Academy of Higher Education, Coimbatore, India; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Karpagam Academy of Higher Education, Coimbatore, India
Publication Title: 2025 9th International Conference on I-SMAC (IoT in Social, Mobile, Analytics and Cloud) (I-SMAC)
Abstract: Digital twins are rapidly becoming a rigorous framework for water-quality monitoring, converting noisy pH and total dissolved solids (TDS) measurements into reliable, decision-ready signals. This review adopts a deliberately architecture-centric lens spanning edge, fog, and cloud to examine how communications (MQTT/HTTP; LPWAN/cellular), compute placement, and orchestration (containers, device shadows, CI/CD) influence accuracy, latency, resilience, and maintainability. We consolidate sensing fundamentals and error modes, then organize data assimilation around state-space modeling: Kalman variants (KF/EKF/UKF), Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoothing, and particle filters, augmented with robust residual tests, Huber-style losses, gap imputation, and multi-sensor fusion using temperature and conductivity for pH compensation. On the decision layer, we compare standards-aligned thresholds with hysteresis and TOT logic, probabilistic exceedance based on posterior uncertainty, and change-point detectors such as CUSUM and BOCPD for abrupt events. The survey proposes a reporting checklist and a benchmarking protocol that links twin fidelity to alert quality via continuous errors (MAE/RMSE), event metrics (precision/recall/F1, detection latency, false-alarm rate), and operational SLOs (uptime, MTTA/MTTR). Case-study archetypes, including river intakes, reservoir buoys, groundwater wells, and treatment plants, are mapped to constraints in power, bandwidth, staffing, and risk tolerance, yielding context-specific design guidance. We conclude with open challenges in drift adaptation, explainability at the edge, cybersecurity, and dataset standardization, and outline a reference setup for reproducible ablations and fair, apples-to-apples comparison.
Author Keywords: Digital twins;Water-quality monitoring;pH/TDS;State-space modeling;Kalman filtering;Change-point detection;Edge-fog-cloud architecture;MQTT/LoRaWAN telemetry

Authors: C. Anderson; T. G. Walmsley; P. Patros

Publication Title: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Autonomic Computing and Self-Organizing Systems Companion (ACSOS-C)
Abstract: The digital twin paradigm is a promising enabling technology to accelerate the decarbonisation of industrial sites that use process heat. With digital representations that look-like, behave-like, and connect to a physical system, digital twins bring together critical operational and asset data into a single knowledge store. However, a high-fidelity digital twin relying on the cloud in real-time with direct influence on operations exposes the plant to cyber attacks. We propose a software architecture for a Digital Twin that adaptively generates more accurate representations of its operations to detect malicious activities and mitigate their effects. To achieve this adaptivity, our solution leverages ML, time-series forecasting, concept drift detection and control stability analysis. To evaluate our solution, we develop a simulation of a simple industrial plant consisting of one PID-controlled steam-boiler and a variety of uncertainties. Our experimental evaluation suggests that Dynamic Mode Decomposition with Control, a system identification technique, best contributes towards Self-Learning by producing verifiable models that better align the need for retraining with concept drifts.

Document Title: Robust Field-Focused Digital Twin for Real-Time Water-Quality Estimation and Alerting
Author Affiliations: Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Karpagam Academy of Higher Education, Coimbatore, India; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Karpagam Academy of Higher Education, Coimbatore, India
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Smart Electronic Devices and Intelligent Systems (ICSEDIS)
Abstract: Sensors and communications should be model-driven in the digital twin that itself accurately represents control logic, so the treatment plant has accurate sanitation evaluations for assimilation decisions (and alarm notifications) even store-and-forward hours later. This work presents a high-fidelity and hardware-realistic digital twin framework to model probe physics, temperature-dependent conductance, reference-electrode drift, telemetry loss, fouling, biofilm-growth mechanism, and the maintenance cycles in order to quantify estimator and alarm performance under normal operational stressors. The twin closes a research gap by integrating a parametric state-space model with a hybrid assimilation toolchain: lightweight Kalman updates for near-real-time denoising, Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoothing for retrospective optimization, and robust residual screening for outlier rejection/gap filling. An alert engine uses standards-aligned thresholds, hysteresis, and time-over-threshold (TOT) rules (with continuous monitoring of residuals using Cumulative SUM [CUSUM] statistics at individual sensor nodes), as well as residual-driven CUSUM and Bayesian online change-point detection to trade off early warning versus nuisance reduction. Results for semisynthetic scenarios calibrated to reservoir, treatment plant, and wellfield conditions are presented, showing reductions of 48.6% in RMSE for pH and 42.3% for TDS; a decrease of the false alarm rate from 12.4% to 3.1%; and a mean reduction of detection delay as high as 38%. The platform consists of a reusable field-focused testbed for algorithm selection, calibration planning, operational SLO development, and operator training guidance.

Document Title: Bio360: A Multimodal Framework for Health Digital Twin Modeling and Early Physiological Drift Detection
Authors: S. Karnati; S. Mukherjee; S. Dasiga
Author Affiliations: Clarksburg High School, Clarksburg, MD, USA; Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, USA; Department of ECE, Nitte Meenakshi Institute of Technology, Bangalore, India
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 14th International Conference on Healthcare Informatics (ICHI)
Abstract: Continuous physiological monitoring through wearable devices and digital health applications has become increasingly prevalent; however, clinically meaningful interpretation of these signals remains limited due to fragmented data ecosystems, heterogeneous sampling characteristics, and reliance on isolated threshold-based alerts. This paper presents Bio360, a multimodal Health Digital Twin (HDT) framework designed to integrate wearable biosignals, health and fitness applications, nutrition and lifestyle inputs, and longitudinal clinical data into a unified, continuously evolving digital health representation. The framework emphasizes longitudinal analysis, personalized baseline-relative interpretation, and contextual multisignal convergence rather than isolated physiological measurements. Bio360 incorporates a four-pillar multimodal architecture supported by a harmonization and normalization pipeline capable of integrating heterogeneous physiological streams across wearable platforms with differing temporal resolutions, signal fidelity, and device-specific schemas. The system further introduces a Contextual Event Evaluator (CEE) that aggregates baseline-relative deviations, signal weighting, and trend persistence into a composite Event Confidence Score (ECS) for identifying potentially meaningful physiological drift. To strengthen predictive interpretation under uncertainty, the framework incorporates Bayesian probabilistic modeling that continuously updates confidence estimates as new physiological and contextual data become available. A representative cardiovascular monitoring scenario demonstrates how persistent convergence among elevated resting heart rate, reduced heart rate variability, altered sleep architecture, behavioral stress patterns, laboratory biomarkers, and family history may collectively indicate emerging physiological risk despite individually nominal measurements. Bio360 further extends beyond physiological modeling through the introduction of a Behavioral Digital Twin (BDT), which incorporates adherence, behavioral routines, and wellness engagement into the broader digital twin ecosystem. The proposed framework aims to support early physiological drift detection, simulation-driven predictive health modeling, and scalable longitudinal health intelligence for future preventive healthcare systems.
Author Keywords: Multimodal Health Monitoring;Wearable Biosensors;Event-Driven Risk Detection;Health Digital Twin;Predictive Health Modeling;Remote Patient Monitoring

Document Title: AI-Driven Soft Sensors: Applications, Validation, and Metrological Challenges
Authors: P. S. Nzakuna; M. Eyunkoel Lasaba; V. Basemenane; E. Mutelezi; V. Paciello; A. K. Lusala
Author Affiliations: Industrial Engineering, University of Salerno, Fisciano, Italy; Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Kinshasa, Kinshasa, DR Congo; Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Kinshasa, Kinshasa, DR Congo; Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Kinshasa, Kinshasa, DR Congo; Industrial Engineering, University of Salerno, Fisciano, Italy; Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Kinshasa, Kinshasa, DR Congo
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence for Instrumentation and Measurement (AI4IM)
Abstract: AI-assisted soft sensors (also called virtual or inferential sensors) estimate difficult-to-measure variables from readily available measurements when direct sensing is impractical due to cost, latency, intrusiveness, or reliability constraints. Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning have expanded soft sensing from classical regression-based estimators to high-capacity models capable of learning nonlinear relationships from multivariate time series and heterogeneous sensor streams. However, deploying these models as measurement functions raises challenges beyond mere point accuracy. Key metrological hurdles include uncertainty quantification, drift under changing operating conditions, sparse reference measurements, data synchronization, and lifecycle governance for model recalibration. This paper reviews the application landscape of AI-assisted soft sensors across industrial processes, manufacturing, energy systems, environmental monitoring, and biomedical sensing, and organizes existing approaches into a practical taxonomy spanning classical machine learning, deep sequence models, hybrid/grey-box methods, online adaptation, and uncertainty-aware modeling. We then synthesize the key metrological challenges that determine trustworthiness in practice: traceability, validation protocols, uncertainty reporting, robustness to distribution shift, and data integrity; and propose a concise evaluation and reporting checklist to improve comparability and reproducibility. Finally, we outline emerging directions such as self-supervised learning, conformal prediction, physics-informed hybrids, and federated learning to support reliable soft sensing across devices, sites, and time.
Author Keywords: artificial intelligence;soft sensors;virtual sensors;deep learning;uncertainty quantification

Document Title: Learning-Based NMPC Adaptation for Autonomous Driving Using Parallelized Digital Twin
Authors: J. P. Allamaa; P. Patrinos; H. Van der Auweraer; T. D. Son
Author Affiliations: Siemens Digital Industries Software, Leuven, Belgium; Department of Electrical Engineering (ESAT)—STADIUS Research Group, KU Leuven, Leuven, Belgium; Siemens Digital Industries Software, Leuven, Belgium; Siemens Digital Industries Software, Leuven, Belgium
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology
Abstract: In this work, we focus on the challenge of transferring an autonomous driving (AD) controller from simulation to reality (Sim2Real). We propose a data-efficient method for online and on-the-fly adaptation of parametrizable control architectures such that the target closed-loop performance is optimized while accounting for uncertainties such as model mismatches, changes in the environment, and task variations. The novelty of the approach resides in leveraging black-box optimization enabled by executable digital twins (xDTs) for data-driven parameter calibration through derivative-free methods to directly adapt the controller in real time (RT). The xDTs are augmented with domain randomization (DR) for robustness and allow for safe parameter exploration. The proposed method requires a minimal amount of interaction with the real world as it pushes the exploration toward the xDTs. We validate our approach through real-world experiments, demonstrating its effectiveness in transferring and fine-tuning a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) with nine parameters, in under 10 min. This eliminates the need for hours-long manual tuning and lengthy machine learning training and data collection phases. Our results show that the online adapted NMPC directly compensates for the Sim2Real gap and avoids overtuning in simulation. Importantly, a 75% improvement in tracking performance is achieved, and the Sim2Real gap over the target performance is reduced from a factor of 876 to 1.033.

Authors: A. A. Al-Hameed; A. S. Alhazmi; S. H. Younus; A. J. Showail; M. A. Ahmed
Author Affiliations: Department of Communication Engineering, College of Electronics Engineering, Ninevah University, Mosul, Iraq; Department of Computer Science and Information, Applied College, Taibah University, Madinah, Saudi Arabia; Department of Communication Engineering, College of Electronics Engineering, Ninevah University, Mosul, Iraq; Department of Computer Engineering, College of Computer Science and Engineering, Taibah University, Madinah, Saudi Arabia; Department of Communication Engineering, College of Electronics Engineering, Ninevah University, Mosul, Iraq
Publication Title: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
Abstract: AI-driven xApps for Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) energy saving achieve substantial power reductions, but they operate as opaque models. Operators cannot audit their decisions, decompose them for cross-xApp conflict negotiation, or constrain them against physically unsafe actions under distribution shift. This paper proposes the Energy-Saving Neural Additive Model (ES-NAM), an inherently interpretable architecture for a near-real-time RAN Intelligent Controller xApp that performs multi-level Advanced Sleep Mode (ASM) control. Unlike opaque models and post-hoc explainability approaches, ES-NAM decomposes each sleep decision into independent, auditable per-feature shape functions, organized into three physically grounded groups: traffic load, radio coverage, and operational history. Hard monotonicity constraints, enforced through softplus weight reparameterization, guarantee that physically unsafe actions such as deep-sleeping a heavily loaded cell cannot occur. The guarantee holds independently of the training data. A cumulative link ordinal head preserves the natural ordering of sleep levels, and group-level attribution scores enable a tunable protocol for evidence-based conflict resolution with co-deployed xApps. On a 57-cell O-RAN-compliant simulation, ES-NAM achieves comparable energy-saving performance of opaque models baselines and achieves zero monotonicity violations on out-of-distribution data. On a 10,000-scenario conflict-resolution evaluation with held-out validation and test splits, the attribution-based protocol achieves 99.5% override precision at the data-driven operating point. Cross-dataset validation confirms that these structural guarantees transfer to unseen network conditions.
Author Keywords: Open RAN (O-RAN);explainable AI (XAI);network energy saving;neural additive models (NAM);advanced sleep modes (ASM);xApp;interpretable machine learning
